pastEvents.name: Grain-a-thon 3.0
pastEvents.description: Spanning five impactful days, Grain-a-thon 3.0 brought together students of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering in a heartfelt effort to combat hunger and promote sustainability. Through an interdepartmental grain donation drive, over 11,672 kg of grains were collected, packed, and distributed to NGOs across Mumbai , reflecting the power of unity and compassion in action.
pastEvents.longDescription:
Grain-a-thon 3.0 was more than just a donation drive, it was a journey of kindness, teamwork, and shared purpose. The college truly breathed life as students from every department joined hands to contribute grains for a noble cause. What began as an interdepartmental competition soon turned into a collective mission, as classrooms and corridors echoed with energy, and the spirit of giving.

Over the course of the drive, heaps of rice and wheat poured in with each packet representing someone’s prosperous tomorrow . Volunteers worked tirelessly to organize and sort every contribution, ensuring that no grain went to waste. The sense of unity grew stronger when students came together to pack not only the collected grains but also donated clothes and e-waste, preparing them for distribution with care and responsibility.

The most rewarding part commenced when volunteers personally visited NGOs across Mumbai to hand over the donations. The smiles, gratitude, and heartfelt interactions they experienced made every effort worthwhile. It was a humbling reminder that even small acts, when multiplied by many, can create a profound impact.

Through Grain-a-thon 3.0, DJSNSS community once again proved that change starts when compassion meets action and that together, we can nourish not just lives, but hope also.
pastEvents.location: Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering, Vile Parle (W)

pastEvents.name: Bhajan Sandhya – A Confluence of Non-Violence and Service
pastEvents.description: A university-level event organized by NSS to promote the ideals of non-violence, peace, and social awareness through bhajans, prayers, and a rally commemorating Gandhi Jayanti.
pastEvents.longDescription:
On the eve of Gandhi Jayanti, October 1, 2025, the University of Mumbai’s National Service Scheme (NSS) organized “Bhajan Sandhya – A Confluence of Non-Violence and Service” at the iconic Gateway of India. The event brought together NSS volunteers from various colleges, including the NSS Unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering (DJSNSS), to spread the message of peace, unity, and civic responsibility.
The day began with an energetic Nashamukti Rally from Azad Maidan at 2:45 p.m., where students passionately advocated the message of “Say No to Drugs,” symbolizing youth commitment toward social well-being. The march culminated at the Gateway of India by 3:40 p.m., where the crowd’s enthusiasm reflected the collective spirit of non-violence and service inspired by Mahatma Gandhi.
Following the rally, the serene Bhajan Sandhya commenced with soulful bhajans, prayers, and peace songs that created an atmosphere of reflection and harmony. The Chief Guest emphasized the importance of non-violence and the fight against drug abuse, reinforcing the relevance of Gandhi’s teachings in modern times. The program concluded with certificate distribution and dispersal at 6 p.m., marking the day as a powerful reminder of youth responsibility, social commitment, and the transformative impact of service.

pastEvents.name: Blood Donation Drive 2025
pastEvents.description: DJSNSS organized a Blood Donation Drive, encouraging students and staff to contribute towards saving lives through the simple yet powerful act of donating blood.
pastEvents.longDescription:
On 26th September, the NSS Unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering (DJSNSS) conducted a Blood Donation Drive at the AIML Department, 4th Floor. The initiative aimed to raise awareness about the importance of blood donation and provide a platform for students and faculty members to contribute to society in a life-saving way.

The event witnessed enthusiastic participation, with students and staff coming forward selflessly to donate blood. Each unit collected has the potential to save multiple lives, making the impact of this initiative profound and far-reaching. Professional medical staff ensured that the process was smooth, safe, and well-organized.

Beyond the act of donating, the drive also fostered a strong sense of responsibility and compassion among the volunteers and donors. It highlighted the importance of community service and how a small contribution from an individual can create a ripple effect of hope and healing.

Volunteers actively assisted in managing the registration process, guiding donors, and ensuring that everyone felt comfortable throughout. Their dedication and energy played a crucial role in the smooth execution of the event.

The Blood Donation Drive was not just a campaign but a testament to the NSS spirit of “Not Me, But You.” It reminded us all that true service lies in giving selflessly for the welfare of others. Together, we created a day that was meaningful, impactful, and full of humanity.
pastEvents.location: Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering, Mumbai

pastEvents.name: Old Age Home Visit
pastEvents.description: DJSNSS volunteers visited old age homes in Borivali, sharing joy, conversations, and companionship with the residents.
pastEvents.longDescription:
On 20th September, the NSS Unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering (DJSNSS) organized an Old Age Home Visit at Mahakali Jan Seva Foundation and Vimalta Devi Foundation in Borivali. The visit was an opportunity for students to step beyond academics and experience the warmth of giving time, attention, and care to the elderly.

Volunteers spent the evening engaging with the residents through conversations, stories, and lighthearted games. Music, laughter, and heartfelt interactions created an atmosphere of joy, bringing smiles to faces and comfort to hearts. While the volunteers aimed to share happiness, they also gained invaluable lessons from the wisdom, experiences, and resilience of the seniors.

The visit served as a gentle reminder of the importance of human connection—how simple gestures like listening, sharing, and being present can make a world of difference. For many volunteers, it was a transformative experience that reinforced the values of empathy, compassion, and respect for our elders.

The event concluded with an overwhelming sense of fulfillment for both the residents and the volunteers. It was not just a day of service but also of reflection, highlighting the responsibility we all share to care for those who once cared for us.

This initiative stands as a testament to the NSS motto, “Not Me, But You,” encouraging selfless service and deeper bonds within our community. 🌟
pastEvents.location: Mahakali Jan Seva Foundation & Vimalta Devi Foundation, Borivali, Mumbai

pastEvents.name: Mangrove Cleaning
pastEvents.description: DJSNSS volunteers came together on 19th September at Bandra to clean mangroves, restoring Mumbai’s natural shield against floods and climate change.
pastEvents.longDescription:
On 19th September, the NSS Unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering (DJSNSS) conducted a Mangrove Cleaning Drive at Bandra, Mumbai. The initiative focused on preserving and restoring one of the city’s most critical ecosystems—the mangroves. These natural guardians not only protect the coastline from erosion and floods but also serve as vital carbon sinks and support rich marine biodiversity.

Equipped with gloves, garbage bags, and an unyielding spirit, our volunteers worked tirelessly to clear out plastic and other waste that had accumulated among the mangrove roots. The drive served as both an environmental action and a powerful reminder of the urgent need to reduce pollution at its source.

The teamwork, energy, and dedication of our volunteers were the true driving force behind the success of this activity. Beyond cleaning, the drive instilled a deeper sense of environmental responsibility in everyone involved.

This was more than just a cleaning drive—it was a pledge to protect what protects us. By taking small yet significant steps, we can collectively build a cleaner, safer, and more sustainable tomorrow.

pastEvents.name: Juhu Beach Cleaning Drive
pastEvents.description: In a meaningful community service initiative, 84 volunteers from Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering came together to clean up Juhu Beach,after the ganesh visarjan removing a significant amount of waste  and promoting environmental awareness.
pastEvents.longDescription:
The event began at 7:00 AM on September 7th, 2025, transforming a simple morning into a truly meaningful experience. As the volunteers arrived at Juhu Beach, they were greeted by the jarring sight of the shoreline a stark contrast to the beautiful scenery. The NSS heads  divided the 84 participants into  groups of 13-15  members each. Each group was equipped with gloves and masks, along with designated gunny bags for collecting waste. The volunteers showed unwavering dedication, diligently working to remove debris, from plastic bottles and bags to discarded flowers and idols left over from celebrations.
The drive was more than just a cleanup; it was devotion and an educational experience. Participants were encouraged to reflect on the immense damage that improper waste disposal causes to our environment. The collaborative nature of the event fostered a strong sense of community and responsibility among the students. By the end of the two-hour drive, a substantial amount of waste had been collected, leaving the beach noticeably cleaner and demonstrating the power of collective action. The event served as a powerful reminder of our role in protecting the environment and a strong commitment to sustainable living.

pastEvents.name: Orphanage Visit – A Journey to the Heart of Hope
pastEvents.description: A heartfelt visit to Catherine Orphan Home, Andheri West, where 74 NSS volunteers spent quality time with children, spreading joy through games, music, and conversations.
pastEvents.longDescription:
The afternoon of August 13, 2025, unfolded into a truly meaningful experience as the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering visited Catherine Orphan Home, Andheri West, from 2 pm to 4 pm. The visit created a lasting impression as we witnessed the resilience and warmth of the children, combined with the dedication of the sisters, caretakers, and staff.

Upon arrival, we were introduced to the head, sisters, caretakers and the overall staff. They shared with us how the children come to the orphanage. Many are found in unsafe or vulnerable situations and are brought in with the help of social workers and authorities. Once here, they are given not just food and shelter, but also education, guidance, and most importantly, love. Hearing these stories made us realize the depth of care behind every smile we saw that day.

Initially, the children were hesitant to interact, but as the session progressed, laughter and joy filled the atmosphere. Volunteers organized games, played Antakshari, and shared a jamming session of songs, making the children feel loved and celebrated. The event beautifully concluded with moments of shared happiness, reminding the us of our social responsibility.

This visit was not just about spending time but about instilling hope and realizing the role we all play in shaping a better tomorrow. It encouraged volunteers to extend empathy, spread joy, and continue working towards creating a more inclusive and caring society.
pastEvents.location: Catherine Orphan Home, Andheri West, Mumbai

pastEvents.name: Independence Day Rally 2025
pastEvents.description: The NSS unit of DJ Sanghvi College celebrated the 79th Independence Day with a flag hoisting ceremony, inspiring address, and a rally promoting unity and patriotism.
pastEvents.longDescription:
The NSS Unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized an Independence Day celebration on 15th August 2025 to honor 79 years of India’s freedom. The program began at 9:00 a.m. with the hoisting of the national flag, which was followed by the singing of the National Anthem. The moment created a collective spirit of pride and togetherness among all participants.

An address was then delivered by Hari Vasudevan Sir, who emphasized India’s achievements since independence and the responsibilities of the youth in building the nation’s future. His words encouraged the volunteers to channel their energy and skills into meaningful service.

The event further featured an Independence Day Rally, where NSS volunteers participated with enthusiasm and carried the message of unity, patriotism, and social responsibility into the community. The celebration concluded at 1:00 p.m., with 40 volunteers actively contributing to the success of the program.

This Independence Day celebration not only highlighted the values of freedom and solidarity but also reflected the NSS spirit of “Not Me, But You,” reinforcing the importance of service to the nation.

pastEvents.name: Bamboo Products Stall
pastEvents.description: A bamboo products stall organized by DJS NSS to support and promote the work of tribal women artisans.
pastEvents.longDescription:
DJS NSS organized a special stall featuring eco-friendly bamboo products crafted by skilled tribal women, in collaboration with Vikramgad Bamboo Udyog Producer Co. Ltd. The initiative aimed to promote sustainable living while empowering the tribal community through financial independence.

The vision of this initiative is rooted in the empowerment of tribal communities across the nation by encouraging them to embark on the path of Atmanirbharta (self-reliance). Through this stall, students and visitors not only supported a noble cause but also experienced the unique craftsmanship and cultural heritage represented in each bamboo product.

pastEvents.name: Education Drive 2025
pastEvents.description: An engaging education drive in collaboration with the Robin Hood Army, fostering learning through creativity and science for underprivileged children.
pastEvents.longDescription: On Sunday, 13th July 2025, DJS NSS in collaboration with the Robin Hood Army conducted a heartwarming education drive at Loknete Gopinath Munde Shakti Ground, Dahisar West. With over 150 children and 40 enthusiastic volunteers participating, the session was filled with fun, learning, and impact. The day started with an origami workshop, helping kids boost their creativity and coordination through art. This was followed by a live science experiment demonstrating cleanliness using oil, food coloring, and soap, making the learning memorable and fun. The event left both volunteers and children with smiles and valuable lessons in creativity, science, and hygiene.
pastEvents.location: Loknete Gopinath Munde Shakti Ground, Dahisar West

pastEvents.name: Tree Plantation Drive
pastEvents.description: A tree plantation event organized by DJS NSS in collaboration with ConnectFor to promote environmental responsibility and restore urban greenery in Aarey Colony, Mumbai.
pastEvents.longDescription: On 28th June 2025, DJS NSS volunteers joined hands with ConnectFor and other NSS units to conduct a Tree Plantation Drive at Aarey Colony, Mumbai. The initiative brought together junior and senior volunteers from DJ Sanghvi College and beyond. Starting at the Forest Office, participants walked to the nearby temple, where they were briefed by a geologist on Aarey’s ecosystem and plantation techniques. Teams then planted saplings across the forest outskirts and interior, with responsibilities including digging, planting, and cleaning up waste. A total of 70 saplings were planted from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM. The event reinforced environmental values and showcased the power of youth-led collective action for sustainability.

pastEvents.name: Paper Bag Distribution Drive
pastEvents.description: A sustainability-focused drive to distribute paper bags and combat plastic pollution across Mumbai.
pastEvents.longDescription: On 22nd June 2025, DJS NSS in collaboration with ConnectFor organized a city-wide Paper Bag Distribution Drive to combat plastic pollution. A 14-member volunteer team distributed over 2000 paper bags, which were part of a 2.5 lakh paper bag contribution made by students of Gokuldham High School. The event started at MPS Balaram Street Urdu School, Grant Road, and extended to areas like Andheri, Vile Parle, and Borivali. A friendly competition between teams boosted volunteer enthusiasm and engagement. This initiative not only promoted the use of biodegradable alternatives but also spread environmental awareness in the community, showcasing the power of youth-led collaborative action.
pastEvents.location: Grant Road (Start Point) + Andheri, Vile Parle, Borivali (Mumbai)

pastEvents.name: Mahim Beach Clean Up
pastEvents.description: A beach clean-up drive organized on World Environment Day 2025 at Mahim Causeway to combat plastic pollution and promote environmental responsibility.
pastEvents.longDescription:
To commemorate World Environment Day 2025 under the theme "Beating Plastic Pollution", a large-scale clean-up drive was held on 5th June 2025 at the banks of the Mithi River in Mumbai. This initiative was organized by Beach Please and the Commonwealth Youth Council, in collaboration with National Service Scheme (NSS) and My Bharat.

Volunteers gathered at 7:45 AM, and the activity commenced by 8:00 AM. After a safety and waste segregation briefing, volunteers removed 60–80 kg of plastic and non-biodegradable waste from the riverbank. The event not only restored a part of Mumbai’s urban ecosystem but also empowered youth to engage in environmental sustainability.

NSS volunteers played a central role in mobilizing participants, executing the clean-up, and raising awareness, showcasing their dedication to social and ecological responsibility.
pastEvents.location: Mahim Causeway Slope, Mumbai (Mithi River Bank)

pastEvents.name: Education Drive Mahalaxmi
pastEvents.description: A creative and interactive educational session for children including crafts, film screening, games, and performances
pastEvents.longDescription: On 18th April 2025, The Vatsalya Foundation in collaboration with DJS NSS organized an enriching and engaging Educational Drive at Mahalaxmi. The session started with a paper butterfly craft activity aimed at enhancing children's creativity and motor skills. It was followed by an inspiring educational film that promoted perseverance and acceptance. To improve speech clarity and confidence, a fun tongue twister game was held. The event concluded with a dance performance, showcasing the children’s joy and creativity. The drive was filled with learning, laughter, and emotional engagement, making it a memorable and impactful community-led initiative.

pastEvents.name: Blood Donation Drive at Andheri Railway Station
pastEvents.description: A blood donation drive held at Andheri Railway Station on 1st April 2025, in collaboration with Jagjivan Ram Hospital and Indian Railways, where 50 individuals donated blood.
pastEvents.longDescription:
On 1st April 2025, DJSNSS, in partnership with Jagjivan Ram Hospital (Western Railway) Blood Centre and supported by Indian Railways, organized a Blood Donation Drive at Andheri Railway Station, turning one of Mumbai’s busiest spots into a hub of compassion and care.

Despite the bustling crowd, 50 individuals stepped up to donate blood, potentially saving up to 150 lives. 20 DJSNSS volunteers ensured smooth functioning throughout — from registration and medical screening to donation and post-care.

The donations were supervised by qualified doctors from the blood centre, with donors undergoing strict medical checks. Eligible individuals (aged 18–65, weighing over 50 kg) donated under sterile, hygienic conditions. Donors received refreshments, certificates of appreciation, and donor cards, which grant priority access to blood for them or their families for up to a year at Jagjivan Ram Hospital.

The event highlighted not just the power of youth and service but also the lasting impact of a few selfless minutes. It reaffirmed the belief that even in the chaos of city life, "Be the reason for someone’s heartbeat" still rings true.

pastEvents.name: Blood Donation Drive
pastEvents.description: The 19th Annual NSS Blood Donation Drive will be held on 4th March from 8 AM to 6 PM at Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering. This year, all donations will go towards children suffering from thalassemia, a genetic disorder that requires lifelong blood transfusions. Volunteers will assist in event coordination, donor management, and logistics to ensure smooth execution.
pastEvents.longDescription:
DJSNSS is organizing its 19th Annual Blood Donation Drive on 4th March from 8 AM to 6 PM at Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering. For the past 18 years, NSS has been committed to helping those in need through this initiative, ensuring a steady blood supply for critical cases.
This year, the donations will specifically support children suffering from thalassemia, a genetic disorder where the body cannot produce enough healthy blood. These children require blood transfusions every 15 days for their entire lives, making a consistent blood supply vital for their survival. A single donation can make a direct and lasting impact on their well-being.
Volunteers will be responsible for donor registration, guiding participants through the donation process, coordinating with medical professionals, maintaining records, and ensuring post-donation care. They will also assist in managing event logistics, setting up the venue, and providing refreshments to donors.
The event is being conducted in collaboration with a recognized blood bank, ensuring that all safety and medical protocols are followed. As the demand for blood continues to rise, this drive provides an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to society.
pastEvents.location: Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering

pastEvents.name: Laxmarao Inaamdaar Memorial Lecture
pastEvents.description: In honor of a great visionary
pastEvents.longDescription: The Laxmanrao Inamdaar Memorial Lecture is an annual event that honors the legacy of Laxmanrao Inamdaar, a visionary social leader dedicated to community upliftment and social service. Esteemed speakers from various fields are invited to deliver thought-provoking talks on topics of social relevance, sharing insights and experiences that inspire action and foster dialogue on important societal issues. The event serves as a platform to reflect on Inamdaar's values, encouraging civic responsibility and motivating individuals to contribute to the betterment of society.

pastEvents.name: Swachhata hi Seva
pastEvents.description: Cleanliness is service
pastEvents.longDescription: Swacchata Hi Seva is a nationwide cleanliness campaign aimed at encouraging citizens to actively participate in cleaning their surroundings. The event is part of the larger Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, promoting hygiene, sanitation, and cleanliness across the country.

pastEvents.name: Gandhi Jayanti Bhajan Sandhya
pastEvents.description: A tribute to Mahatma Gandhi
pastEvents.longDescription: Gandhi Jayanti Bhajan Sandhya is an annual event held to commemorate the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. The event includes devotional singing sessions, paying homage to the Father of the Nation, and reflecting on his principles of non-violence and truth.

pastEvents.name: Mann Ki Baat
pastEvents.description: A nationwide interaction
pastEvents.longDescription: Mann Ki Baat is a nationwide radio program through which the Prime Minister of India directly addresses the citizens, sharing his thoughts on key issues of national importance. The program serves as a platform to engage and inspire the nation, particularly the youth, by discussing topics that encourage civic participation, social harmony, and national development. It fosters a sense of unity and collective purpose, promoting awareness and action on various social, cultural, and developmental matters affecting the country.

pastEvents.name: VOTER REGISTRATION
pastEvents.description: Your vote, your voice
pastEvents.longDescription: Voter Registration Drive: 'Your Vote, Your Voice' On 15th September 2023, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a voter registration drive to encourage students to exercise their democratic rights. The event, held at DJ Sanghvi College, aimed to raise awareness about the importance of voting and empower students to participate in the electoral process. The drive was a resounding success, with over 300 students registering to vote and many more engaging in informative sessions and interactive activities. The drive featured inspiring speeches, engaging discussions, and interactive games that highlighted the significance of voting in shaping the future of the nation. The event showcased the power of civic engagement and community involvement in promoting democracy and social change. The enthusiasm and commitment of all participants made the drive a memorable and impactful experience, setting the stage for future initiatives to support voter education and participation.

pastEvents.name: Budget Buzz
pastEvents.description: Understanding the Union Budget
pastEvents.longDescription: Budget Buzz is an annual event that aims to educate students about the Union Budget of India. The event features expert speakers who provide insights into the budgetary process, allocations, and policies, helping participants understand the economic implications and significance of the budget for the country. Through interactive sessions and discussions, students gain valuable knowledge about fiscal planning and governance.

pastEvents.name: Stem Cell Donation Drive 2024
pastEvents.description: A stem cell donation drive helps register potential donors to save lives of patients battling blood cancers and other deadly diseases.
pastEvents.longDescription: A Stem Cell Donation Drive is a life-saving initiative aimed at raising awareness and encouraging individuals to register as potential stem cell donors. Stem cells are used to treat over 80 life-threatening diseases, including blood cancers like leukemia and lymphoma. By joining the donor registry, you could be a match for a patient in need of a transplant and give them a second chance at life. The process is simple, non-invasive, and begins with just a cheek swab. Your small act of registration could one day become someone’s hope for survival.
pastEvents.location: Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering

pastEvents.name: GRAIN-A-THON
pastEvents.description: Our small actions, others' huge aid
pastEvents.longDescription: Scarcity to abundance: Grain-a-thon On 15th August 2023, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a Grain-a-thon, a food donation drive to support underprivileged communities. The event, held at DJ Sanghvi College, aimed to raise awareness about food insecurity and encourage students to contribute to this vital cause. The drive was a resounding success, with over 200 volunteers donating grains and other essential food items. The drive featured inspiring speeches, interactive sessions, and engaging activities that highlighted the importance of community service and collective action. The event showcased the power of empathy and compassion in addressing social challenges and fostering a culture of giving. The enthusiasm and generosity of all participants made the drive a memorable and impactful experience, setting the stage for future initiatives to support vulnerable communities and promote social justice.

pastEvents.name: INDEPENDENCE DAY RALLY
pastEvents.description: Celebrating freedom with unity
pastEvents.longDescription: On 15th August 2024, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized an Independence Day Rally, celebrating India's freedom and promoting national unity. The event featured a patriotic march, inspiring speeches, and cultural performances that highlighted the importance of independence and the sacrifices made for the nation. Students, faculty, and volunteers participated enthusiastically, showcasing their love for the country. The rally concluded with a flag-hoisting ceremony and a pledge to uphold the values of democracy, unity, and equality. The event was a significant reminder of the ongoing efforts needed to preserve and protect the nation's freedom and heritage.

pastEvents.name: Meri Mitti Mera Desh
pastEvents.description: Honoring our land and heritage
pastEvents.longDescription: Meri Mitti Mera Desh is a nationwide campaign aimed at instilling pride and respect for the land we live on. The event involves various activities that promote environmental conservation and cultural heritage, encouraging citizens to reconnect with the soil and history of India.

pastEvents.name: TREE PLANTATION
pastEvents.description: Planting trees, planting hope
pastEvents.longDescription: Tree Plantation Drive: 'Meri Mitti Mera Desh' On 9th August 2023, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering successfully organized a tree plantation drive at Veer Savarkar Udhyan, Borivali West. The event, themed 'Meri Mitti Mera Desh', aimed to foster environmental responsibility and raise awareness about the vital role of trees in combating climate change. Around 80 dedicated volunteers, including students and organizers, participated in planting over 110 saplings of native species, carefully chosen to enhance the local ecosystem. The drive began with inspiring speeches, and participants eagerly engaged in planting activities, showcasing their commitment to creating a greener future. The event highlighted the power of collective action and community involvement in environmental conservation. The enthusiasm and teamwork displayed by all contributed to the event's resounding success, marking a significant step toward a sustainable environment.

pastEvents.name: NEWSPAPER COLLECTION DRIVE
pastEvents.description: Recycle today for a better tomorrow
pastEvents.longDescription: On 5th June 2024, World Environment Day, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a Newspaper Collection Drive aimed at promoting recycling and environmental sustainability. The event encouraged students to collect and donate old newspapers, which were then sent for recycling. The drive included educational sessions on the importance of recycling and its impact on reducing waste and conserving resources. The event successfully collected a significant amount of paper waste, highlighting the collective effort needed to protect the environment and promoting a culture of sustainability among the college community.

pastEvents.name: Connect for Sensory Board Event
pastEvents.description: Empowering differently-abled children
pastEvents.longDescription: On 5th April 2024, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a sensory board event in collaboration with Connect, a local NGO. The event aimed to create sensory boards for differently-abled children to aid in their cognitive development. Volunteers crafted and assembled boards with various textures, colors, and objects, providing the children with a valuable tool for learning and sensory stimulation. The event was a fulfilling experience for all involved, fostering creativity and empathy among the volunteers.

pastEvents.name: Versova Beach Cleanup
pastEvents.description: Join hands for a cleaner coast
pastEvents.longDescription: On 18th March 2024, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering conducted a cleanup drive at Versova Beach. The event, which focused on reducing plastic pollution, saw participation from over 60 students. Volunteers worked tirelessly to remove garbage and raise awareness about the detrimental effects of plastic waste on marine life. The event was a significant step towards fostering a cleaner environment and instilling the importance of sustainability among students.

pastEvents.name: Bandra Beach Cleanup
pastEvents.description: Restoring our shores
pastEvents.longDescription: On 12th March 2024, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a Bandra Beach Cleanup drive. The event aimed to restore the natural beauty of the beach and promote environmental awareness. Over 50 volunteers participated, collecting plastic waste and other debris. The cleanup drive not only helped in cleaning the beach but also educated participants on the importance of environmental conservation and waste management.

pastEvents.name: Anti Dowry Rally
pastEvents.description: Rally against the dowry system
pastEvents.longDescription: The Anti Dowry Rally is a significant event aimed at raising awareness about the social evil of the dowry system. The rally involves students, faculty, and volunteers marching together to promote gender equality and social justice, advocating for the eradication of this harmful practice.

pastEvents.name: Cybersavvy
pastEvents.description: Navigating the digital world safely
pastEvents.longDescription: On 28th February 2024, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering held a workshop aimed at educating students about online safety and digital literacy. The workshop covered topics such as cybersecurity, online privacy, and safe social media practices. Experts in the field provided valuable insights, and interactive sessions allowed participants to ask questions and discuss real-world scenarios. The event was well-received and equipped students with the knowledge needed to navigate the digital world safely and responsibly.

pastEvents.name: Juhu Beach Cleanup
pastEvents.description: Keeping our beaches pristine
pastEvents.longDescription: The NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a cleanup drive at Juhu Beach on 25th February 2024. The event focused on removing litter and raising awareness about the impact of pollution on marine ecosystems. Volunteers participated enthusiastically, collecting several bags of waste. The event not only contributed to a cleaner beach but also helped instill a sense of responsibility towards environmental conservation among participants.

pastEvents.name: ANNUAL CHARITY DRIVE
pastEvents.description: Shaping India's futures
pastEvents.longDescription: From February 20th to 24th, DJ Sanghvi College of Engineering became a center of compassion and creativity during the DJSNSS Annual Charity Drive. This event united volunteers and the college community in a mission to raise funds for specially-abled children.The drive was a resounding success, raising over Rs 75,000 to support three NGOs: Kshitij, based at Charni Road, and Purnavas and VDIS, both in Malad. These funds will significantly aid the organizations in their ongoing efforts to nurture the talents of these children. The event featured a vibrant showcase of handcrafted items made by the children, including handmade chocolates, earrings, anklets, bracelets, and jute bags. Ganpati idols, symbolizing new beginnings, were also on display. Purchasing these items did more than raise funds; it celebrated the talents of these children, affirming their value and creativity. The Annual Charity Drive wasn’t just about raising money—it was a celebration of community spirit and collective kindness. In those five days, DJ Sanghvi College became a place where every contribution helped create a world where everyone’s abilities are recognized. The DJSNSS Annual Charity Drive showed that when we give from the heart, we enrich lives and build a tapestry of kindness that touches us all.

pastEvents.name: BLOOD DONATION DRIVE
pastEvents.description: Donate blood, save lives
pastEvents.longDescription: Set up for success: Blood Donation Drive On 14th February 2023, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized a blood donation drive in collaboration with the Red Cross Society. The event, held at DJ Sanghvi College, aimed to raise awareness about the importance of blood donation and encourage students to contribute to this life-saving cause. The drive was a resounding success, with over 100 volunteers donating blood and many more participating in the event. The drive featured informative sessions on the benefits of blood donation, dispelling myths and misconceptions and inspiring participants to make a difference. The event showcased the power of collective action and community involvement in saving lives and promoting health and well-being. The enthusiasm and dedication of all participants made the drive a memorable and impactful experience, setting the stage for future initiatives to support public health and welfare.

pastEvents.name: NSS Camp
pastEvents.description: A camp to remember
pastEvents.longDescription: From January 26 to 31, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering organized an enriching camp at Dahanu, focusing on community service and personal growth. The camp kicked off with cleanliness drives, team-building activities, and creative tasks like poster making and wall painting, all fostering a spirit of teamwork and community engagement. Throughout the week, volunteers participated in impactful initiatives, including educational outreach, a medical camp, and environmental awareness drives. The installation of solar street lights highlighted the camp's commitment to sustainability. The camp concluded with cultural celebrations and a strong sense of accomplishment among participants, leaving a lasting impact on the community and volunteers alike.

pastEvents.name: Orphanage Visit
pastEvents.description: Spreading smiles and joy
pastEvents.longDescription: On 14th January 2024, the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering visited an orphanage in Andheri. The visit aimed to bring joy to the children by organizing fun activities, games, and a small gift distribution. Volunteers spent quality time with the children, engaging in meaningful interactions that left a lasting impact on both the visitors and the children. The event highlighted the importance of compassion and community service in making a difference in the lives of the less fortunate.

pastEvents.name: Aabhar 2022
pastEvents.description: Celebrating the spirit of gratitude
pastEvents.longDescription: Aabhar 2022, held on 20th December 2022, was a heartwarming event organized by the NSS unit of Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering to express gratitude towards the unsung heroes of the society. The event featured performances by students, heartfelt speeches, and the distribution of appreciation tokens to sanitation workers, security personnel, and other support staff. The event was a beautiful reminder of the importance of acknowledging and appreciating those who work behind the scenes to make our lives better.
